topic: The ask-vs-infer discipline (human-for-feasibility): default to inference when the choice is documented anywhere; ask only when undocumented AND the cost of being wrong exceeds the cost of interrupting

subtopics.scope: The economics of the question: every prompt is an interruption, the polite-yes failure mode, why the right default is inference, and the cost of inferring wrong.
queries: polite yes sycophancy AI assistant users agree to questions
cost of interruption context switching knowledge workers research

subtopics.scope: When the discipline applies explicitly (low tolerance signals, non-interactive contexts, ship-mode) and when it must NOT be applied (explicit consultation, irreversible severe decisions, genuinely unclear intent).
queries: AI agent autonomous decision making when to ask human permission
levels of human oversight AI agents autonomy

subtopics.scope: The evidence ladder: user's latest message, prior turns, memory, loaded skills, workspace artifacts, prior sessions; implicit answers count as documented.
queries: LLM agent check context memory before asking user clarification
agent retrieve conversation history memory before question

subtopics.scope: Sensible defaults from engineering, project, and industry convention and the skill ecosystem when no explicit documentation exists.

sensible defaults design principle software engineering

subtopics.scope: Classifying decisions by cost of being wrong: trivially reversible, reversible low cost, reversible high cost, irreversible; the ask threshold per tier.

irreversible production operations guardrails blast radius
